Agent Wingman for OpenCode

No agent goes alone.

A local, detector-first OpenCode plugin that notices repetitive, low-progress work and gives a concise nudge before the loop becomes expensive.

> **Status:** `0.1.0` release candidate. The package is prepared for public npm publishing but is not published yet. This is a community project, not an official OpenCode product. ## Why Agent Wingman Coding agents can repeat the same failing command, revisit the same file or search, restate a plan, or keep consulting without changing the hypothesis. Agent Wingman watches OpenCode's local event stream for those patterns and intervenes only when repetition and low progress occur together. The detector is deterministic and bounded. It does not call another model, upload transcripts, or block tool execution. ## What it does - Observes terminal tool results through both `tool.execute.after` and the stable event stream, deduplicating the two paths. - Observes completed assistant text without treating user prompts as agent struggle. - Detects repeated failures, error-family recurrence, read/search churn, plan repetition, consultation churn, and dense low-progress windows. - Applies confidence scoring, cooldowns, per-episode caps, and global rate limits. - Defaults to a bounded inline synthetic no-reply advisory; notification-only and shadow modes remain available. - Fails open: detector or delivery errors never block OpenCode. - Uses a version-neutral runtime adapter with no OpenCode package dependency or exact-version gate. ## Inline advisory When the detector identifies a high-confidence low-progress loop, Agent Wingman adds a concise synthetic advisory at the session boundary. The message is explicitly marked as plugin-generated and uses `noReply` so it does not start another model turn automatically. ![Agent Wingman synthetic advisory displayed inline in OpenCode](./assets/agent-wingman-synthetic-advisory.png) ## Install ### From source today ```bash git clone https://github.com/spyd3r83/agent-wingman.git cd agent-wingman bun install bun run verify bun run build mkdir -p /path/to/project/.opencode/plugins cp dist/src/index.js /path/to/project/.opencode/plugins/agent-wingman.js ``` OpenCode automatically loads JavaScript files in `.opencode/plugins/` on startup. ### After the first npm release ```bash opencode plugin opencode-agent-wingman ``` Or add it to `opencode.json`: ```json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugin": ["opencode-agent-wingman"] } ``` ## Modes | Mode | Model-visible | Behaviour | |---|---:|---| | `inject` | Yes | Default. Adds a synthetic no-reply advisory and falls back to notify on failure. | | `notify` | No | Shows a warning toast and writes a structured local log. | | `shadow` | No | Logs eligible interventions without displaying them. Good for calibration. | Example with options: ```json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugin": [["opencode-agent-wingman", { "mode": "shadow", "threshold": 9 }]] } ``` See [CONFIGURATION.md](./CONFIGURATION.md) for every bounded option. ## Privacy and safety - No telemetry, external service, persistence, or network call is added by the plugin. - Raw prompts, tool arguments, tool output, source files, and command results are not retained. - Secret-shaped values are redacted before fingerprinting. - Fingerprints use an ephemeral per-process HMAC key, so they cannot be correlated across restarts. - Advisories are fixed templates and never quote untrusted tool output. - Session observations, episode state, and deduplication state all have hard memory bounds. Read [PRIVACY.md](./PRIVACY.md) and [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) for the full boundaries. ## Validation ```bash bun test bun run typecheck bun run trace:replay bun run smoke bun run package:check ``` CI additionally loads the same distributable through real OpenCode minimum, midpoint, and npm `latest` runtimes. If OpenCode is installed locally, `bun run smoke:opencode` runs the same isolated load check. The trace corpus separately enforces precision, recall, and duplicate-intervention gates. See [COMPATIBILITY.md](./COMPATIBILITY.md) for the precise support contract. ## Scope Agent Wingman is advisory. It does not browse, execute tools, mutate files, delegate agents, make access-control decisions, or claim that deterministic detection can identify every unproductive loop. Start in `shadow` mode when evaluating unfamiliar workflows. The default inline advisory is a fixed template marked `synthetic` and `noReply`. It never includes raw prompts, tool arguments, tool output, source text, or command results. Set `mode` to `notify` for user-only delivery or `shadow` for log-only calibration. ## Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). Detection changes need a labelled synthetic trace that explains the false positive or false negative being addressed. ## License Apache-2.0. See [LICENSE](./LICENSE).

# Changelog

All notable changes will be documented here.

## 0.1.0 - Unreleased

- Added bounded, deterministic struggle detection and synthetic trace replay.
- Added stable OpenCode event ingestion with terminal-event deduplication and assistant-only text observation.
- Added a version-neutral structural adapter with no OpenCode runtime, peer, or public type dependency.
- Verified the same artifact against OpenCode `1.3.5`, `1.14.17`, and the latest stable release.
- Corrected stable V1 TUI and no-reply request contracts.
- Added default inline synthetic injection, notification-only and shadow overrides, and fail-open delivery fallback.
- Added real OpenCode CLI load testing, package-content checks, and pinned CI actions.
- Added ephemeral HMAC fingerprints, bounded cross-session state, and public-safe documentation.
- Added an original Agent Wingman vector logo.

# Compatibility

## Compatibility contract

Agent Wingman targets the stable OpenCode V1 plugin contract, beginning with OpenCode `1.3.5`. It has no runtime dependency, peer dependency, exact-version gate, or public declaration import on an OpenCode package.

Compatibility is based on capabilities and structural event data:

- The adapter accepts unknown host values and ignores event shapes it does not understand.
- Tool observations use `tool.execute.after` and the stable event stream, with cross-path deduplication.
- Notifications, logs, and inline injection are attempted only when their client methods exist.
- A missing or changed optional surface degrades to another delivery mode or a no-op; it never blocks OpenCode.

## Continuous verification

| OpenCode lane | Version | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| Minimum | `1.3.5` | Protects the documented support floor. |
| Midpoint | `1.14.17` | Detects compatibility assumptions hidden by endpoint-only testing. |
| Current | npm `latest` | Tests the newest stable release on every pull request. |

Every lane loads the same built JavaScript artifact from `.opencode/plugins/` in an isolated real CLI startup. Unit tests separately exercise event parsing, malformed/unknown input, dual-path deduplication, and delivery contracts. Bun `1.3.14` runs the build and test toolchain.

The package does not use OpenCode's beta V2 plugin API. Default model-facing delivery uses the stable V1 `session.prompt` client with `noReply` and a synthetic fixed-template part. Setting `mode: "notify"`, `mode: "shadow"`, or `experimentalInject: false` disables inline injection. A missing or failing prompt surface falls back to notification.

“Version-neutral” means supported stable V1 releases are selected by capabilities instead of exact version numbers. It does not promise compatibility with pre-`1.3.5` releases, beta APIs, or a future breaking V2 contract. A failure in the npm `latest` lane blocks release until compatibility is restored or the support statement is deliberately revised.

# Configuration

Options may be supplied in the OpenCode plugin tuple. Environment variables are intentionally limited to the operational mode and the two kill-switch style flags.

| Option | Environment | Default | Accepted range |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `enabled` | `AGENT_WINGMAN_ENABLED` | `true` | boolean |
| `mode` | `AGENT_WINGMAN_MODE` | `inject` | `shadow`, `notify`, `inject` |
| `experimentalInject` | `AGENT_WINGMAN_EXPERIMENTAL_INJECT` | `true` | boolean |
| `threshold` | — | `8` | 1–100 |
| `minRelevantActions` | — | `8` | 1–100 |
| `maxSessions` | — | `64` | 1–1024 |
| `maxObservations` | — | `128` | 16–2048 |
| `maxEpisodesPerSession` | — | `64` | 8–1024 |
| `cooldownMs` | — | `300000` | 0–86400000 |
| `maxInterventionsPerEpisode` | — | `2` | 1–20 |
| `maxInterventionsPerWindow` | — | `2` | 1–100 |
| `interventionWindowMs` | — | `1800000` | 1000–86400000 |

Invalid numeric values fall back to defaults; out-of-range numeric values are clamped. Unknown modes fall back to `inject`.

Recommended calibration:

```json
{
  "plugin": [["opencode-agent-wingman", { "mode": "shadow", "threshold": 9 }]]
}
```

Default inline injection:

```json
{
  "plugin": ["opencode-agent-wingman"]
}
```

Notification-only override:

```json
{
  "plugin": [["opencode-agent-wingman", {
    "mode": "notify"
  }]]
}
```

The `experimentalInject` setting remains as a compatibility and emergency kill switch. Setting it to `false` while `mode` is `inject` forces notification delivery. If the host injection surface is missing or fails, delivery also falls back to a TUI notification and then to a structured local log. Detection never blocks the active OpenCode operation.

# Detection model

Agent Wingman intervenes only when it sees repetition plus low progress. A single failure, repeated test with changing evidence, or productive edit loop is insufficient.

| Signal | Initial condition | Score |
|---|---:|---:|
| Exact failed action recurrence | Same action and failure 3 times in the recent window | +4 |
| Failure recurrence | Same normalized error family 3 times | +3 |
| Read or research churn | Same resource or query group 4 times | +2 |
| Zero productive delta | 8 relevant operations without a progress marker | +2 |
| High error density | 5 failures in the last 8 operations | +2 |
| Plan repetition | Same completed assistant plan 3 times | +1 |
| Consultation churn | Same consultation 3 times without a successful edit | +2 |
| Successful resolution | Previously failing action succeeds | -5 |
| Meaningful change | Successful edit occurs | -2 |
| New evidence | New resource or outcome appears | -2 |

Scores below 8 remain observational. Scores from 8–10 are intervention-eligible; 11 or higher is high confidence. The default policy permits no more than two interventions per episode and two interventions per 30-minute window, with a five-minute cooldown.

Episode keys and resource identities are ephemeral keyed fingerprints. They are useful only within one process and are not stable analytics identifiers.

## Known limitations

Deterministic signals can miss semantic loops and can over-collapse distinct work when normalized actions are very similar. Assistant-text detection waits for terminal text parts and therefore does not react mid-sentence. The labelled replay corpus and real OpenCode load smoke are gates, not proof that every workflow is correctly classified.

# Privacy

Agent Wingman is local and memory-only by default.

- No telemetry or remote service.
- No added external network calls.
- No persistence or transcript collection.
- No raw prompt, tool argument, tool output, source file, or command result retained in detector state.
- No untrusted output copied into an advisory.

The detector retains bounded in-memory observations containing coarse event and tool classes, success status, timestamps, fixed explanations, and fingerprints. Secret-shaped values are redacted before fingerprinting. Fingerprints use a random per-process HMAC key, so the same input produces unrelated identifiers after restart and cannot be correlated between installations.

OpenCode's own storage, session retention, and logging behaviour is outside this plugin's boundary. Every delivery mode writes structured local OpenCode logs containing signal names, confidence, scores, and keyed episode identifiers—not raw event material. The default inline mode also adds a fixed synthetic advisory to the OpenCode session; it does not copy raw prompts, tool arguments, tool output, source text, or command results.

Any future persistence, telemetry, or diagnostic export would require a documented threat model, explicit opt-in, retention controls, and a separate public review before release.

# Security policy

## Supported versions

Until `0.1.0` is released, only the latest commit on `main` receives security fixes. After release, the latest `0.1.x` version will be supported.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Do not open a public issue for a suspected secret leak, unsafe model-facing injection, prompt-injection path, dependency compromise, or data exposure.

Use GitHub's **Security → Report a vulnerability** flow for this repository. Include the affected version or commit, synthetic reproduction steps, observed impact, and whether any credential or private content may have been exposed. Do not include real secrets or private transcripts.

## Security invariants

- Tool execution and permissions are never blocked or approved by Agent Wingman.
- Advisories use fixed templates and never quote tool output.
- Secret-like values are redacted before keyed fingerprinting.
- Fingerprint keys are random, process-local, and never persisted.
- Model-facing delivery is disabled unless two explicit settings agree.
- Plugin-originated synthetic messages are excluded from detection.
- Session, observation, episode, message-role, and deduplication state are bounded.
- Detector and delivery failures are handled fail-open.

Dependency updates and OpenCode compatibility changes must pass tests, trace gates, type checks, package inspection, and a real CLI plugin-load smoke.

# Asset provenance

`agent-wingman-logo.svg` is an original vector mark created specifically for Agent Wingman. It does not copy the OpenCode logo, a third-party icon set, or another product mark.

The asset contains only static SVG geometry, gradients, and accessibility metadata. It has no scripts, external resources, embedded raster data, fonts, tracking, or network references.

The logo is distributed under the repository's Apache-2.0 license. “Agent Wingman” is a project name; the Apache-2.0 license does not grant trademark rights.
